case_name: State of Andhra Pradesh and Ors. v Mcdowell and Company And Ors.
petitioner: State of Andhra Pradesh and Ors
facts: The Government prohibited the sale and consumption of intoxicating liquors by an Ordinance issued on December 27,1994.
In February, 1995, the Legislature of Andhra Pradesh enacted the Andhra Pradesh Prohibition Acts, 1995 [hereinafter referred to as "the Act"] replacing the Ordinance.

The long title and the preamble to the Act reads: "An Act to introduce Prohibition of the Sale and Consumption of intoxicating liquors in the State of Andhra Pradesh and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto."

Several licencees approached the High Court of Andhra Pradesh by way of writ petitions challenging the provisions of the Act and seeking a declaration that the Act does not prohibit the manufacture of liquor, though it may well prohibit the sale and consumption thereof.
The full Bench, which heard the writ petitions, agreed with the writ petitioners.
Against the judgment of the Full Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court, the State of Andhra Pradesh preferred Special Leave Petitions (C) Nos.13936-13941 of 1995.
On July 18, 1995, the Governor of Andhra Pradesh issued Ordinance No.12 of 1995 amending certain provisions of the Act.

The manufacturers of intoxicating liquors in Andhra Pradesh have now come forward with these writ petitions u/art. 32 of the Constitution of India challenging the Constitutional validity of Act 35 of 1995 [hereinafter referred to as the "amending Act"].
issues: Whether the Act prohibits the manufacture of liquor within the State of Andhra Pradesh.
Whether the amending Act is beyond the legislative competence of the Andhra Pradesh Legislature.
petitioner_arguments: The Act does not prohibit the manufacture of liquor though it may well prohibit the sale and consumption thereof.
The prohibition of possession of liquor in Section 7, the Full Bench opined, was only for the purpose of consumption, selling and buying within the State and does not affect the manufacture.
respondent_arguments: The Act prohibits the manufacture of liquor within the State of Andhra Pradesh.
The amending Act is within the legislative competence of the Andhra Pradesh Legislature.
court_reasoning: The prohibition of possession of liquor in Section 7, the Full Bench opined, was only for the purpose of consumption, selling and buying within the State and does not affect the manufacture.
The amendment to the definition of 'liquor' in cl. (7) of S. 2 of the Act includes Indian liquor and Foreign liquor.
holding: The judgment of the Full Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court is upheld, and the amending Act is declared unconstitutional.
